description: Which diagnosis --REASON_FOR--> service relations may satisfy medical necessity. A relation authored by the same extraction model that authored the events is not, by itself, independent clinical support: it must be evidence-anchored in the source document, clear the confidence floor, and carry a reconciliation status that was established DETERMINISTICALLY -- re-assertion from DISTINCT recorded assertion origins (a repetition inside one response is one origin and counts once), or a clause of the source that states the relationship DIRECTIONALLY. Bare co-location of the two facts in one passage is recorded but is NOT accepted: it proves both were documented together, never that one is the reason for the other. Every released service needs such a linkage; where an authoritative coverage policy governs the service the qualifying-diagnosis check is an ADDITIONAL requirement on that same linked diagnosis, never a substitute for it.
authority: Social Security Act 1862(a)(1)(A) -- services must be reasonable and necessary for the diagnosis or treatment of illness or injury
CMS Program Integrity Manual (Pub. 100-08) Chapter 3, Section 3.3.2.1.1 -- the medical record must support the medical necessity of the service billed
CMS Medicare Claims Processing Manual (Pub. 100-04) Chapter 23 -- diagnosis-to-service linkage on the claim
notes: The corroboration THRESHOLD is not declared here: it belongs to the reconciliation layer that reads it (claude_coder/controls/relation_evidence_grammar.json, min_independent_assertions). It was declared here in v1 and consumed by nobody, so raising it would silently have changed nothing. Thresholds and accepted statuses are configuration, not code, so a control change is a reviewed config diff. Nothing here is a medical code, code family, or descriptor proxy: it is a relation-evidence control. Loading is fail-closed -- a missing or malformed control file makes the necessity gate ERROR (autonomy stops) rather than falling back to a built-in default. 'source_colocated' was REMOVED from the accepted set in v2: it records co-occurrence, which is not a directional clinical proposition (Codex F6-R3).
